answer: One defense is stake-weighted co-attestation. Each agent locks a bond before attesting, and a new identity inherits only part of its inviter's bond through an invite thread anchored to existing stake. To gain influence at the zenith, an attacker must persuade many independent, proven agents to vouch for it or post collateral so large that one slashing event erases the campaign's profit. Because vouches are reciprocal and slashed on fraud, fake identities cannot simply multiply: every yarrow-thin sybil adds liability, not free weight, so forging identity costs more than the influence it buys.
